family_title: Selective and sparse fine-tuning (train a chosen subset of the existing parameters)

methods.name: BitFit
methods.paper_title: BitFit: Simple Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning for Transformer-based Masked Language-models
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0 x + (b_0 + \Delta b),\quad W_0,\ g_{LN}\ \text{frozen};\ \text{trainable: every bias vector } \Delta b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ (Q/K/V/O, MLP and LayerNorm biases) plus the task head}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\ \text{per linear layer (its bias)};\ \approx 0.08\text{--}0.09\%\ \text{of BERT parameters}
methods.locus: bias vectors only (attention Q/K/V/O, MLP, LayerNorm biases); LayerNorm gains and all weight matrices frozen
methods.structure: \Delta W = 0; only the translation part of each affine map h = Wx + b moves, i.e. a fixed, hand-specified coordinate mask on \theta that selects exactly the bias coordinates
methods.mergeable_reason: The tuned biases are the model's own bias parameters, so the fine-tuned model has exactly the original architecture and cost.
methods.identity_at_init: Biases start at their pretrained values (\Delta b = 0), so the function is unchanged at initialization.
methods.key_idea: Freezing all weights and fine-tuning only the additive bias terms (plus the classifier) of a pretrained Transformer is competitive with full fine-tuning on small and medium datasets; tuning only the query and middle-MLP biases (0.04% of parameters) loses little.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with BERT-base/large, bias-only tuning is comparable to full fine-tuning and to Diff Pruning/Adapters while training under 0.1% of parameters; it is strongest in small-to-medium data regimes.

relations.note: BEFT restricts bias tuning further, to the value-projection bias only.
Both tune only per-channel affine parameters already present in the network (shift vs. LayerNorm scale/shift).
(IA)^3 learns new multiplicative per-channel scalings, BitFit tunes the existing additive per-channel shifts.
Both are sparse difference vectors; BitFit fixes the support a priori, Diff Pruning learns it.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2106.10199 (Ben-Zaken, 2021-06; comment 'ACL 2022 main') and ACL Anthology 2022.acl-short.1 confirmed. Bias set (incl. LayerNorm biases, gains g frozen), 0.09%/0.08% of BERT-base/large and the 0.04% b_q+b_m2 ablation match Sec. 2-4. HF PEFT main (v0.21.1, tuners dir listed via GitHub API) has no BitFit tuner; LoraConfig(bias='all') only co-trains biases with LoRA.

methods.name: Diff Pruning
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning with Diff Pruning
methods.formula_latex: \theta_\tau = \theta_0 + \delta_\tau,\quad \delta_\tau = z_\tau\odot w_\tau,\quad \min_{\alpha_\tau,w_\tau}\ \mathbb{E}_{z_\tau\sim p(z;\alpha_\tau)}\big[\mathcal{L}(\theta_0+\delta_\tau)\big] + \lambda\sum_i \sigma\!\big(\alpha_{\tau,i}-\log\tfrac{-l}{r}\big);\ \text{then keep the top } t\% \text{ of } |\delta_\tau| \text{ and re-train with the mask fixed; } \theta_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2\,d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{during training } (w,\alpha);\ \ \|\Delta W\|_0\approx 0.005\,d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{stored (0.5\% target)}
methods.locus: all pretrained parameters (embeddings, weight matrices, biases); structured variant groups gates per weight matrix / bias vector
methods.structure: learned sparse coordinate mask: \Delta W = Z\odot V with Z a stretched Hard-Concrete relaxation of a binary gate (differentiable L_0 penalty), projected onto an L_0 ball by magnitude pruning of the diff; optional group gates z^{g} shared within each weight matrix/bias vector
methods.mergeable_reason: The final diff vector is added to the pretrained parameters, giving an ordinary model of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: w_\tau initialized to 0 so \delta_\tau = 0; gate logits \alpha_\tau initialized to 5 so that z \approx 1 at the start.
methods.key_idea: Treat fine-tuning as learning a task-specific diff vector added to frozen pretrained weights and make it sparse with a relaxed L0 penalty, so each new task costs only a small sparse vector.
methods.results_note: Structured Diff Pruning matches full fine-tuning of BERT-large on GLUE while modifying only 0.5% of parameters per task.

relations.note: FISH Mask precomputes the support from Fisher information instead of learning it, avoiding Diff Pruning's dense training memory.
LT-SFT obtains the support from the largest changes of a dense fine-tuning pass instead of a relaxed L0 gate.
Masking learns a binary mask on the weights themselves (W_0 \odot M); Diff Pruning learns a masked additive update W_0 + Z \odot V.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2012.07463 (Guo, 2020-12) and ACL 2021 (2021.acl-long.378) confirmed. Objective, stretched Hard-Concrete gate, expected-L0 term sigma(alpha - log(-l/r)) with l=-1.5, r=1.5, init w=0 / alpha=5, L0-ball magnitude projection and fixed-mask re-finetuning all match Sec. 3; structured groups are per matrix/bias vector (393 groups for BERT-large).

methods.name: FISH Mask
methods.paper_title: Training Neural Networks with Fixed Sparse Masks
methods.formula_latex: \hat F_i = \tfrac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_\theta(y|x_n)}\big(\partial_{\theta_i}\log p_\theta(y|x_n)\big)^2,\quad M = \mathbb{1}\big[\hat F \ge \mathrm{sort}(\hat F)_k\big],\quad W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W,\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \eta\,(M\odot\nabla_W\mathcal{L})
methods.trainable_params: k\ \text{in total (one global top-}k\text{ over all parameters, e.g. } k = 0.005\,|\theta|\text{)};\ \text{per-matrix counts vary because the mask concentrates in some layers}
methods.locus: any parameter; top-k diagonal-Fisher coordinates selected globally across the network (classifier always included)
methods.structure: fixed sparse coordinate mask chosen once before training as the top-k entries of the diagonal (empirical) Fisher information, then reused for all iterations
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing parameters change, so the result is a standard dense model of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Training starts at the pretrained weights (\Delta W = 0); the Fisher is computed through the randomly initialized classifier before any training.
methods.key_idea: Estimate each parameter's importance by its diagonal Fisher information on a few samples, pick the top-k, and train only those with a mask that never changes.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with BERT, updating 0.5% of parameters with a FISH Mask matches standard training and outperforms Diff Pruning, Adapters and random/bias masks; also reduces communication in distributed training.

relations.note: Precomputed Fisher mask vs. learned L0-relaxed mask; FISH avoids Diff Pruning's extra training memory.
Child-Tuning_D (the task-driven variant) uses the same rule: a fixed mask of the top empirical-Fisher entries; the two papers are concurrent (2021).
PaFi replaces the Fisher criterion by a data-free, task-agnostic smallest-magnitude rule.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2111.09839 (Sung, 2021-11); NeurIPS 2021 confirmed in the proceedings listing. Eq. 3 (diagonal Fisher averaged over N samples, expectation over y ~ p_theta), the top-k rule {theta_i : F_i >= sort(F)_k}, classifier always included and Fisher computed through the random head all match Sec. 2. Selection is a single global top-k.
corrections: trainable_params: k is one global top-k over all parameters, so the per-matrix figure rho*d_out*d_in was not accurate; rewritten as a global count.
relations: restricted the equivalent-to note on child-tuning to its task-driven variant Child-Tuning_D (Child-Tuning_F is a random per-step mask).

methods.name: Child-Tuning
methods.paper_title: Raise a Child in Large Language Model: Towards Effective and Generalizable Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta\,\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}(w_t)}{\partial w_t}\odot M_t;\quad \text{Child-Tuning}_F:\ M_t\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_F)\ \text{(kept gradients scaled by } 1/p_F);\quad \text{Child-Tuning}_D:\ M = \mathbb{1}\big[F^{(i)} \in \text{top-}p_D\big],\ F^{(i)} = \tfrac{1}{|D|}\sum_j\big(\partial_{w^{(i)}}\log p(y_j|x_j;w)\big)^2,\ \text{fixed for all } t
methods.trainable_params: \text{Child-Tuning}_D:\ p_D\,|\theta|\ \text{in total (one global top-}p_D\text{ Fisher threshold; per-matrix counts vary)};\ \ \text{Child-Tuning}_F:\ \text{expected } p_F\,|\theta|\ \text{per step, every entry can change over training}
methods.locus: all pretrained parameters (masks applied to gradients inside the optimizer, e.g. AdamW)
methods.structure: Hadamard gradient mask: a fixed top-p_D diagonal-Fisher mask (task-driven, genuinely selective) or a fresh Bernoulli(p_F) mask every step (task-free); the task-free variant accumulates a dense update and acts as a gradient-noise regularizer rather than a parameter-efficient method
methods.mergeable_reason: It only changes which existing parameters are updated; the fine-tuned network has the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; no new parameters.
methods.key_idea: Update only a 'child network' of the pretrained model: a random Bernoulli subset each step acts as a variance-increasing regularizer favouring flat minima, while a Fisher-selected fixed subset targets task-relevant parameters.
methods.results_note: On GLUE, Child-Tuning outperforms vanilla fine-tuning by 1.5-8.6 average points across four PLMs (BERT, XLNet, RoBERTa, ELECTRA) and improves out-of-domain generalization.

relations.note: Child-Tuning_D's fixed top empirical-Fisher mask is the FISH Mask rule; concurrent 2021 works.
LT-SFT selects by largest change after dense fine-tuning rather than by Fisher information.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2109.05687 (Xu, 2021-09) and EMNLP 2021 (2021.emnlp-main.749) confirmed. Eq. 3 masked update, Bernoulli(p_F) mask with 1/p_F rescaling, empirical-Fisher Eq. 10 and the fixed C_0 = ... = C_T child network for the D variant all match Sec. 2. The official ChildTuningD.py takes one percentile over all parameters, so selection is global.
corrections: trainable_params: Child-Tuning_D thresholds the Fisher scores of all parameters at one global percentile (official ChildTuningD.py), so the count is p_D*|theta| overall, not p_D*d_out*d_in per matrix.
structure: added that Child-Tuning_F's per-step random mask accumulates a dense update (a training-procedure regularizer), so only Child-Tuning_D is selective in the sense of this family.

methods.name: LT-SFT
methods.paper_title: Composable Sparse Fine-Tuning for Cross-Lingual Transfer
methods.formula_latex: \text{Phase 1: } \theta^{(1)} = \mathrm{FT}(\theta^{(0)}),\ \mu = \mathbb{1}\big[\,|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(0)}| \in \text{top-}K\big];\ \ \text{Phase 2: reset to } \theta^{(0)},\ \text{train with } \mu\odot\nabla_\theta\mathcal{L},\ \phi = \theta^{(2)}-\theta^{(0)};\ \ \text{composition: } F(\cdot;\theta^{(0)}+\phi_T+\phi_L)
methods.trainable_params: K\ \text{in total (one global top-}K\text{; e.g. } K \approx 7.6\text{M} = 4.3\%\ \text{of mBERT for language SFTs, 0.25--8\% for task SFTs);\ per-matrix counts vary}
methods.locus: all Transformer parameters, including the input embeddings; for language SFTs the output embedding matrix is decoupled and frozen and LayerNorm parameters are frozen; the task classifier head is trained densely in both phases
methods.structure: sparse difference vector \phi supported on a lottery-ticket mask (top-K largest absolute change after a dense fine-tuning pass); SFTs act on the parameter space by translation, so they compose additively: S_L \circ S_T = translation by \phi_T + \phi_L
methods.mergeable_reason: Each SFT is a sparse vector added to the pretrained weights; any sum of SFTs is again a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Phase 2 restarts from the pretrained values (\phi = 0); optional L1 penalty \tfrac{\lambda}{N}\sum_i|\theta_i-\theta_i^{(0)}| keeps the deltas small.
methods.key_idea: Borrow the lottery-ticket recipe (train, select, rewind, retrain) to find a sparse set of parameters per language and per task; because the resulting deltas are sparse they can be added together with little interference, giving adapter-like modularity with full expressivity.
methods.results_note: In zero-shot cross-lingual transfer (POS, dependency parsing, NER, NLI) with mBERT/XLM-R, LT-SFT outperforms MAD-X adapters, e.g. +2.5 POS accuracy and +3.7 LAS.

relations.note: Same language-adapter/task-adapter composition scheme, but realised by adding sparse deltas instead of stacking adapters.
Same sparse-difference-vector formulation; the support is chosen by lottery-ticket selection.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07560 (Ansell, 2021-10) and ACL 2022 (2022.acl-long.125) confirmed. Two-phase procedure, top-K |theta1-theta0| mask, masked-gradient phase 2, optional L1 term lambda/N sum|theta-theta0| and additive composition S_L o S_T all match Sec. 3. Selection is a global top-K.
corrections: locus: the paper does not exclude embeddings; it freezes the decoupled output embedding and LayerNorm parameters during language SFT (Sec. 4) and trains the classifier head densely.
trainable_params: K is a global top-K, so the per-matrix rho*d_out*d_in figure was replaced by the global count and the paper's K values.
relations: removed 'generalizes spiel' (wrong direction: SpIEL is the later method that scales sparse fine-tuning to LLMs; the lineage is already recorded as spiel builds-on lt-sft).

methods.name: SPT
methods.paper_title: Sensitivity-Aware Visual Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: s_n = \textstyle\sum_{c=1}^{C} g_{n,c}^2\ \ (g_{n,c} = \partial E/\partial w_n \text{ on sample } c;\ \text{one-step Taylor estimate of the loss reduction}),\ \ \mathcal{T} = \text{top-}\tau(s),\ M_{ij}=\mathbb{1}[W_{ij}\in\mathcal{T}];\quad W = \begin{cases} W_0 + BA, & \|M\|_0 \ge \sigma_{opt}\ \text{(structured tuning)}\\ W_0 + M\odot\Delta W, & \text{otherwise (unstructured tuning)}\end{cases}
methods.trainable_params: \|M\|_0\ \text{(unstructured) or } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(LoRA on sensitive matrices)},\ \text{under a global budget } \tau
methods.locus: ViT weight matrices; positions chosen per task by gradient-squared sensitivity
methods.structure: per-matrix choice between a sparse coordinate mask (top-\tau gradient-squared sensitivity) and a low-rank (LoRA) or adapter update on matrices that contain many sensitive entries
methods.mergeable_reason: SPT-LoRA and the unstructured part merge into W_0; the SPT-Adapter variant keeps inserted adapter modules.
methods.identity_at_init: Unstructured part starts at Delta W = 0; structured part uses the zero-initialized LoRA/adapter of the host method. Sensitivity is accumulated in one pass over C = 800 training samples before training (400 are shown to suffice).
methods.key_idea: Measure, per task and before training, how much tuning each pretrained weight would reduce the loss (approximated by its squared gradient), then spend the parameter budget there, upgrading heavily sensitive matrices to low-rank or adapter tuning.
methods.results_note: With ViT-B/16, SPT-Adapter/SPT-LoRA reach state of the art on FGVC and VTAB-1k (e.g. +4.2% and +1.4% mean top-1 over Adapter) and transfer to MAE/MoCo v3 backbones and segmentation.

relations.note: Structured branch is LoRA (or an adapter) applied only to the sensitive matrices.
GPS also selects by gradient magnitude on ViT but enforces K entries per neuron and stays purely sparse.
SPT's unstructured criterion (sum of squared gradients) is the empirical-Fisher diagonal that FISH Mask ranks by, derived independently via a Taylor argument; SPT does not cite FISH.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.08566 (He, Haoyu; 2023-03; comment 'ICCV 2023 Oral') and Crossref (ICCV 2023) confirmed. Sensitivity s_n = sum of squared per-sample gradients (Alg. 1, one-step Taylor argument, Eq. 1-3), top-tau budget, Eq. 5 switch to LoRA/adapter when the count of sensitive entries in a matrix reaches sigma_opt all match Sec. 3. Main experiments use C = 800 samples.
corrections: formula_latex: the sensitivity sums squared gradients over C samples (s_n = sum_c g_{n,c}^2); the old notation sum_c g_n^2 had no sample index.
identity_at_init: main experiments use C = 800 samples for the sensitivity (400 is the ablation showing it suffices), not ~400.
relations: fish-mask builds-on -> competes-with; SPT does not cite FISH Mask, it only arrives at the same squared-gradient score.

methods.name: PaFi
methods.full_name: PaFi (task-agnostic sparse fine-tuning of smallest-magnitude weights)
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning without Introducing New Latency
methods.formula_latex: M = \mathbb{1}\big[\,|W_0| \le \mathrm{sort}(|W_0|)_k\big]\ \text{(per matrix, data-free, shared by all tasks)},\quad W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W;\ \text{norm-layer parameters fully trained, embeddings frozen}
methods.trainable_params: k\ \text{per matrix};\ \text{default } k = 0.005\,d_{out}d_{in}
methods.locus: every weight matrix and bias vector (group-wise bottom-k), plus all normalization parameters
methods.structure: fixed sparse coordinate mask on the k smallest-magnitude pretrained entries of each matrix; one universal mask for every downstream task
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing entries are changed in place, so inference uses the original dense model with no latency overhead.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta W = 0 at the start; the mask needs no data or training.
methods.key_idea: The least important pretrained weights (smallest magnitude) are the safest to repurpose, so one data-free mask can be reused for every task, removing the task-specific mask-generation stage of sparse fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with RoBERTa-large, PaFi reaches 89.3 average (equal to full fine-tuning) with 0.5% trainable parameters, at least 1.3 points above Diff Pruning and FISH Mask.

relations.note: Replaces task-specific Fisher selection with a task-agnostic magnitude rule.
Super-Tuning's magnitude-only BottomK support is exactly a PaFi-style mask; its Wanda variant reweights |W| by activation norms.
Both store sparse deltas; PaFi needs only one mask for all tasks.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.16742 (Liao, 2023-05; comment 'ACL2023 camera-ready') and ACL 2023 (2023.acl-long.233) confirmed. Bottom-k |theta| mask chosen group-wise (each weight matrix or bias vector is a group), normalization layers fully trained, token/position embeddings frozen, 0.5% budget and GLUE 89.3 avg (= Full FT, vs 87.9 Diff Pruning / 88.0 FISH) all match Sec. 3-4.
corrections: code_url: canonical GitHub owner casing is BaohaoLiao/pafi_hiwi.

methods.name: SMT
methods.paper_title: SMT: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models with Sparse Matrices
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Delta W_M,\quad \mathrm{supp}(\Delta W_M) = \bigcup_{b\in\mathcal{B}} \text{block}_b,\ \ \mathcal{B} = \text{top-}m\ \text{of } \operatorname{mean}_{(i,j)\in b}\Big|\sum_{t\le T_w}\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_t\Big|_{ij}\ \text{over } l\times l \text{ blocks } (l=256)
methods.trainable_params: m_W\, l^2\ \text{per selected matrix } (m_W \text{ selected } l\times l \text{ blocks, } l=256;\ \text{blocks ranked jointly over all Q/K/V matrices});\ 0.84\%\text{--}4.91\%\ \text{of parameters in the experiments}
methods.locus: attention W_q, W_k, W_v (mainly W_v); MLP layers frozen
methods.structure: block-sparse mask: \Delta W is nonzero only on a set of selected l\times l sub-matrices (tiles), gathered into a dense m\times l\times l tensor so compute stays dense
methods.mergeable_reason: Updated sub-matrices are slices of the original weights; the fine-tuned model is a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; blocks are chosen after a short gradient warm-up (about 25-100 iterations).
methods.key_idea: Select whole sub-matrices with the largest accumulated gradients during a short warm-up and update only those blocks, which keeps the sparsity hardware-friendly and avoids the rank plateau of low-rank methods.
methods.results_note: On commonsense and arithmetic reasoning with LLaMA-7B/13B, LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B, SMT outperforms DoRA (e.g. +3.0/+2.8 on commonsense for LLaMA-7B/13B) and does not plateau as the trainable budget grows.

relations.note: Block-sparse instead of low-rank update at matched budget; avoids LoRA's performance plateau at large rank.
Main baseline; SMT reports consistent gains over DoRA.
Both select by gradient magnitude; SMT selects contiguous blocks, SIFT individual entries.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2405.15525 (He, Haoze; 2024-05) exists under the title 'Sparse Matrix in Large Language Model Fine-tuning'; the ICLR 2025 camera-ready title used here is confirmed on the ICLR 2025 virtual site (poster 30274), which links OpenReview GbgCRJedQ7. Block score (mean |summed warm-up gradient| over 256x256 tiles), Q/K/V-only with MLP frozen, 100 (commonsense) / 25 (Math10K) warm-up steps match Sec. 3-4.
corrections: trainable_params: replaced 'typically <5%' with the budgets actually reported (0.84%-4.91%) and noted that blocks are ranked jointly across Q/K/V matrices.

methods.name: SpIEL
methods.full_name: Sparse Iterative Efficient Learning (sparse fine-tuning with drop-and-grow)
methods.paper_title: Scaling Sparse Fine-Tuning to Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \theta' = \theta + \mathrm{scatter}(\eta,\phi,d_\theta),\ \ \Delta W = \mathrm{reshape}(\mathrm{scatter}(\eta,\phi));\ \text{every } S \text{ steps: drop } \arg\mathrm{top}k(-|\phi|),\ \text{grow } \arg\mathrm{top}k\,\big|\hat{\mathbb{E}}_{x}[\nabla_\theta\mathcal{L}(x;\theta')]\big|\ \text{(SpIEL-AG) or by SM3 momenta (SpIEL-MA)}
methods.trainable_params: d_\phi = \rho\,d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{per matrix (same density for every tensor) plus } d_\phi \text{ indices}
methods.locus: all linear-layer weight tensors of an LLM (embeddings excluded)
methods.structure: dynamic sparse coordinate set: an index vector \eta and value vector \phi, updated by RigL-style drop (smallest |\phi|) and grow (largest accumulated gradient or approximate momentum); memory O(d_\phi)
methods.mergeable_reason: The final delta is scatter-added into the pretrained weights, producing a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: \phi = 0 and \eta a random index subset (all of it is replaced at the first update).
methods.key_idea: Make sparse fine-tuning memory-efficient for LLMs by storing only indices and deltas and letting the support evolve during training through drop-and-grow, instead of computing a dense mask up front.
methods.results_note: Instruction-tuning LLaMA 2 7B/13B on Flan v2, GPT4-Alpaca and Tulu v2, SpIEL is often better than LoRA and (IA)^3 at comparable run time and is compatible with 4-bit quantization and SM3.

relations.note: Same group and sparse-delta formulation; removes the need for a dense first fine-tuning phase.
Main LLM-scale baseline.
SHiRA is concurrent; it uses a static mask whereas SpIEL's mask is dynamic.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.16405 (Ansell, 2024-01) confirmed. No venue found (not in ICML 2024/2025, NeurIPS 2024, ICLR 2024/2025 listings; Semantic Scholar lists arXiv), so venue stays arXiv. scatter-add parametrization (Eq. 5), equal density per parameter tensor, drop argtopk(-|phi|), grow by gamma-step accumulated gradients (AG) or SM3 momenta (MA), random initial eta fully replaced at the first update match Sec. 3. Embeddings are not adapted (listed as future work).

methods.name: LN Tuning
methods.paper_title: Tuning LayerNorm in Attention: Towards Efficient Multi-Modal LLM Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{LN}(x) = \gamma\odot\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}+\beta\ \ \big(\mathrm{RMSNorm}: \gamma\odot x/\mathrm{RMS}(x)\big);\ \text{train only } \gamma,\beta \text{ of the input and post-attention norms of every block; all } W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 4dL\ \text{(two LayerNorms with gain and bias per block) or } 2dL\ \text{(RMSNorm gains only), plus } d \text{ for the final norm};\ \text{LLaMA-2-7B: } 2\cdot 4096\cdot 32 \approx 0.26\text{M} \approx 0.004\%
methods.locus: LayerNorm / RMSNorm gains (and biases) inside each Transformer block; in the paper's default the vision-language connector, embeddings and LM head are also trainable ('LayerNorm-simp.' freezes them)
methods.structure: diagonal per-channel scaling (and shift) of normalized hidden states; since diag(\gamma) precedes a linear map, it is equivalent to rescaling the input columns of the next W: W\,\mathrm{diag}(\gamma)
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing normalization parameters change, so the architecture and inference cost are unchanged.
methods.identity_at_init: \gamma and \beta start from their pretrained values.
methods.key_idea: Turning an LLM into a multimodal LLM behaves like domain adaptation, and within each attention block tuning only the LayerNorm parameters suffices, rivalling LoRA and full fine-tuning at a fraction of the parameters.
methods.results_note: On a 13B MLLM, LayerNorm tuning improves over LoRA by more than 20% on average across five multimodal tasks while cutting trainable parameters by 41.9% and GPU memory by 17.6%.

relations.note: Both tune per-channel affine parameters that already exist (norm scale/shift vs. linear biases).

Changing a pre-norm gain gamma is a right multiplication of the next projection, W diag(gamma) (input-channel scaling); (IA)^3 scales outputs, diag(l) W (left multiplication). The two are transposes of each other.
Main baseline in the MLLM setting.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2312.11420 (Zhao, Bingchen; 2023-12) confirmed; ICLR 2024 confirmed on the ICLR 2024 virtual site (OpenReview YR3ETaElNK). LayerNorm-only tuning inside attention blocks, LayerNorm-simp. (0.004% of a 7B MLLM) and the 41.9% / 17.6% savings match the paper. HF PEFT LNTuningConfig confirmed (tuners/ln_tuning, docstring cites 2312.11420); default targets for llama are input_layernorm, post_attention_layernorm and the final norm.
corrections: url: pointed to the ICLR 2024 OpenReview forum (YR3ETaElNK) instead of the arXiv abstract.
trainable_params: added the final norm and a check against the paper's 0.004% figure for the 7B RMSNorm model.
relations: made the dual-to note on ia3 precise (right vs left diagonal multiplication).

methods.name: LISA
methods.paper_title: LISA: Layerwise Importance Sampling for Memory-Efficient Large Language Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{every } K \text{ steps: } \mathcal{S}_t = \{\text{embedding}, \text{LM head}\}\cup\{\gamma \text{ layers sampled from } N_L \text{ with } p_\ell = \gamma/N_L\};\ \ \theta_{\mathcal{S}_t}\leftarrow\mathrm{AdamW}(\theta_{\mathcal{S}_t}),\ \theta_{\overline{\mathcal{S}_t}} \text{ frozen};\ \ \{p_\ell\} = \{1,\gamma/N_L,\dots,\gamma/N_L,1\}
methods.trainable_params: \text{per period: } |\theta_E| + |\theta_H| + \gamma\cdot|\theta_{\text{layer}}|;\ \text{all parameters can change over training}
methods.locus: whole Transformer layers (embedding and LM head always active; gamma intermediate layers resampled every K steps)
methods.structure: time-varying layer-block coordinate mask (randomized block-coordinate AdamW); the accumulated \Delta W is dense and full-rank
methods.mergeable_reason: It performs full-parameter updates on the original architecture; the result is an ordinary model.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; no new parameters. Optimizer states exist only for the currently active layers.
methods.key_idea: LoRA's layer-wise weight-norm profile is dominated by the embedding and head layers, so emulate it in full-parameter training by always training those and randomly unfreezing a few middle layers at a time, giving LoRA-level memory with full-rank updates.
methods.results_note: On instruction tuning (7B-70B models), LISA outperforms LoRA by 10%-35% on MT-Bench and can match or beat full fine-tuning, with memory comparable to LoRA.

Designed as a memory-equivalent but full-rank alternative to LoRA.

methods.name: GPS
methods.paper_title: Gradient-based Parameter Selection for Efficient Fine-Tuning

methods.trainable_params: K\,d_{out}\ \text{per matrix (K input connections per neuron; } \approx 0.36\%\ \text{on average)}
methods.locus: every weight matrix of the backbone (ViT, Swin, ConvNeXt), all layers; gradients computed with a supervised contrastive loss
methods.structure: row-balanced sparse mask: exactly K nonzeros in every row of \Delta W, so each neuron's activation can be adjusted through its K most gradient-relevant input connections
methods.mergeable_reason: Only selected entries of existing weights change; inference uses the unchanged architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights (\Delta W = 0); selection uses a supervised contrastive loss so that no randomly initialized head biases the gradients.
methods.key_idea: Pick, for every neuron, the few incoming weights with the largest task gradient, which spreads the budget over all layers instead of concentrating it at the top, and train only those.
methods.results_note: On FGVC and VTAB-1k with ViT-B/16, GPS improves over full fine-tuning by 3.33% and 9.61% mean accuracy while tuning 0.36% of parameters on average.

methods.name: S²FT
methods.paper_title: S²FT: Efficient, Scalable and Generalizable LLM Fine-tuning by Structured Sparsity
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W = U_S V^{\top},\ \ U_S = [e_{a_1},\dots,e_{a_s}]\ \text{a frozen one-hot channel selector},\ V \text{ trainable};\ \text{in practice: the slices of } W_O \text{ belonging to selected heads } S_{MHA} \text{ and of } W_{down} \text{ belonging to selected FFN channels } S_{FFN}, \text{ co-permuted to be contiguous}

methods.identity_at_init: Selected slices start at their pretrained values (\Delta W = 0); selection is random by default (S²FT-R) or by weight, activation, weight×activation or gradient magnitude.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2412.06289 (Yang, Xinyu; 2024-12) confirmed; NeurIPS 2024 confirmed in the proceedings listing. Delta W = U_S V^T with a frozen one-hot U_S (Sec. 4, 'a LoRA variant that fixes U_S'), random selection by default (S2FT-R), co-permutation of coupled structures, and the choice of the output and down projections all match the paper.

methods.name: SIFT
methods.paper_title: Sparse is Enough in Fine-tuning Pre-trained Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \mathcal{S} = \text{top-}x\%\ \text{coordinates of } |g_1|\ (\text{gradient of the first batch(es)}),\quad W = W_0 + \Delta W,\ \ \mathrm{supp}(\Delta W)\subseteq\mathcal{S},\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \eta\,P_{\mathcal{S}}(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_t)

methods.mergeable_reason: The sparse increment is added into the existing weights.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta W = 0; support fixed after the first batch.

methods.name: HiFT
methods.paper_title: HiFT: A Hierarchical Full Parameter Fine-Tuning Strategy
methods.formula_latex: \theta = (\theta_{G_1},\dots,\theta_{G_k})\ \text{(k groups of m layers)};\ \text{at step } t \text{ update only } \theta_{G_{\pi(t \bmod k)}} \text{ with any optimizer (others frozen, their optimizer states offloaded)};\ \text{learning rate advanced once per full cycle}

methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; no new parameters.

relations.note: Deterministic cyclic vs. randomized layer selection.

methods.name: SHiRA
methods.paper_title: Sparse High Rank Adapters

methods.name: Surgical FT
methods.paper_title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
methods.formula_latex: \theta = (\theta_{B_1},\dots,\theta_{B_n});\ \text{fine-tune only } \theta_{B_j} \text{ (one contiguous block), others frozen};\ \text{Auto-RGN: per-tensor learning rate } \propto \mathrm{RGN} = \|g\|_2/\|\theta\|_2 \text{ normalized to } [0,1]
methods.trainable_params: |\theta_{B_j}|\ \text{(one block of layers)}
methods.locus: one contiguous block of layers: first block for input-level shift, middle blocks for feature-level shift, last layer for output-level shift
methods.structure: layer-block coordinate mask: \Delta W nonzero only on the weights of one contiguous block (soft version: per-tensor learning rates from relative gradient norms)

methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained (source) model; no new parameters.
methods.key_idea: Which layers to fine-tune should depend on where the distribution shift lives: tuning only early layers fixes input-level shifts, middle layers feature-level shifts, and the head output-level shifts, often beating full fine-tuning.

methods.paper_title: BAdam: A Memory Efficient Full Parameter Optimization Method for Large Language Models

methods.name: Masking
methods.full_name: Learning binary weight masks instead of fine-tuning

methods.full_name: Piggyback (learning to mask weights of a fixed backbone)

methods.name: RoSA
methods.paper_title: RoSA: Accurate Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Robust Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA + S,\quad \mathrm{supp}(S)\subseteq M,\ \ M = \mathrm{TopK}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal{D}_M}(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_s)^{\alpha}\big|_{W_0+\tilde B\tilde A},\ d\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\Big),\ \alpha\in\{1,2\},\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0 \text{ frozen};\ \tilde B\tilde A = \text{LoRA after a 64-batch warm-up}

methods.identity_at_init: LoRA is first trained alone for 64 batches to compute the mask, then training restarts with both adapters at BA = 0 (B = 0) and S = 0; the mask is fixed from then on.
methods.key_idea: Full fine-tuning updates are not low-rank but are well approximated by low-rank plus sparse, so train both components jointly with system support for sparse adapters.
methods.results_note: Fine-tuning LLaMA2-7B on GSM8K, ViGGO and SQL generation, RoSA outperforms LoRA and pure sparse adaptation at equal budget and can match full fine-tuning.

relations.note: Adds a sparse component to LoRA.
Sparse component uses a FISH-like accumulated-gradient mask.
SPT chooses sparse or low-rank per matrix; RoSA uses both on every matrix.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.04679 (Nikdan, 2024-01) confirmed; ICML 2024 confirmed in PMLR v235 (nikdan24a). Eq. 5 (rank <= r plus ||S||_0 <= d m n), Alg. 1 mask (32 samples, alpha in {1,2}, per-matrix TopK), 64-batch LoRA-only warm-up, then restart with LoRA + sparse adapter, densities 0.15-2.4% match Sec. 3 and 5.
corrections: formula_latex: mask gradients are taken at W_0 plus a briefly warmed-up LoRA (64 batches) and alpha is in {1,2}; both were missing.
identity_at_init: described the LoRA-only warm-up used for mask generation and the restart of training with both adapters at zero.

methods.name: BEFT
methods.paper_title: BEFT: Bias-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Language Models in Low-Data Regimes
methods.formula_latex: h_v = W_v x + (b_v + \Delta b_v),\quad \text{only } \Delta b_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ (value-projection bias) is trained; for bias-free LLMs a zero-initialized } \Delta b_v \text{ is added}
methods.trainable_params: d_{v}\ \text{per value projection (its output width)};\ d_{v}L\ \text{per model} = dL \text{ without grouped-query attention}\ (\approx 0.01\%\ \text{of BERT-base})
methods.locus: value-projection bias b_v in every attention layer
methods.structure: translation of the value vectors only: a single per-channel additive shift of W_v x in each layer
methods.mergeable_reason: Merges into the existing value bias. Because softmax rows sum to 1, Delta b_v is also equivalent to an output-projection bias W_o Delta b_v (paper App. B.2), but bias-free models such as LLaMA have neither bias, so a bias must be added to fold it (HF PEFT refuses to merge then).
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta b_v initialized to 0.
methods.key_idea: Among bias terms, the value bias is the one whose fine-tuning best predicts downstream gains (once angular as well as magnitude changes are considered), so tuning b_v alone gives extreme parameter efficiency in low-data regimes.
methods.results_note: Across BERT-base, OPT-1.3B and LLaMA2-7B (up to 6.7B parameters) on classification, multiple-choice and generation tasks, tuning b_v beats tuning b_q or b_k in low-data regimes with about 0.01% of parameters.

relations.note: A one-bias-type restriction of BitFit.
The paper also applies LoRA/VeRA/DoRA-style reparameterizations to the bias terms.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2509.15974 (Huang, Baichuan; 2025-09) and ACL 2026 (2026.acl-long.1799) confirmed. b_v-only tuning, zero-initialized b_v added to bias-free LLMs (Sec. 3.6), ~0.01% of BERT-base parameters, combination with LoRA/VeRA/DoRA (App. C.4) match the paper. HF PEFT BeftConfig confirmed (added in v0.20.0): one zero-initialized vector per targeted Linear, default targets v_proj/value, merge raises if the base layer has no bias.
corrections: trainable_params: the count is the value projection's output width d_v, which is smaller than d under grouped-query attention (e.g. LLaMA-3), so dL was replaced by d_v L.
mergeable_reason: added the paper's equivalence Delta b_v ~ output bias W_o Delta b_v, which is why folding still needs a bias somewhere.

methods.name: Super-Tuning
methods.full_name: Super / Supra: activation-aware sparse fine-tuning (and its LoRA hybrid)
methods.paper_title: Super-Tuning: From Activation-Aware Pruning to Sparse Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: A_{ij} = |W_{0,ij}|\,\|X_{j:}\|_2\ (\text{Wanda score from a calibration pass}),\ \ M = \mathrm{TopK}_s(A)\ \text{or}\ \mathrm{BottomK}_s(A),\quad \text{Super: } W = W_0 + M\odot U;\ \ \text{Supra: } W = W_0 + M\odot U + \gamma\,LR
methods.trainable_params: s\ \text{per matrix (Super)};\ s + r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(Supra)}
methods.locus: LLM linear layers. HF PEFT: default targets copy LoRA's; scores are |W_0| only (no Wanda); defaults are sparsity = 0.99 (1% trainable) and select_top = True (TopK), whereas the paper's strongest rows use BottomK
methods.structure: fixed sparse coordinate mask from a pruning saliency score (activation-weighted magnitude), optionally summed with a LoRA term
methods.mergeable_reason: Both the sparse values and the optional LoRA term are additive and foldable into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Sparse values U initialized to 0 and LoRA B = 0 (HF PEFT init_weights=True).
methods.key_idea: Reuse pruning saliency (Wanda) to decide where to adapt: the scores that say which weights can be removed also identify a good fixed support for sparse fine-tuning, with no gradient-based selection.
methods.results_note: On Llama-family models fine-tuned on Math17K, Supra (BottomK) gives the best average arithmetic accuracy among tested adapters (62.23% vs 61.07% for LoRA on the 1B model) in single-seed comparisons.

relations.note: The magnitude-only BottomK support is PaFi's rule; Wanda reweights magnitudes by input activation norms.
Supra is a sparse plus low-rank hybrid like RoSA but with a training-free support.
Gradient-based (SIFT) vs. activation-aware magnitude (Super) supports.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2607.09287 (Ilin, 2026-07-10, v1) confirmed; no venue, so arXiv. Wanda score A_ij = |W_ij| ||X_j:||_2 (App. B), TopK/BottomK per-layer support, Super = W + M.U and Supra = W + M.U + gamma L R match Sec. 3. HF PEFT SupertuningConfig (added in v0.21.0) uses |W| scores only (no Wanda), sparsity = 0.99 and select_top = True by default, and lora_alpha = 2r. The paper's best sparse-only Llama-3-8B row is Magnitude (BottomK) at 79.02 vs Supra-Wanda 78.66, while the HF docstring describes it as 'magnitude-topk'. The HF default direction is therefore not the paper's best one.
corrections: locus: recorded the HF PEFT defaults (magnitude score only, sparsity 0.99, select_top=True), which differ from the paper's Wanda score and its best BottomK direction.

methods.name: Trainable Tokens
methods.formula_latex: E = E_0 + P_{\mathcal{I}}\,\Delta E_{\mathcal{I}},\quad \text{only the rows } \{E_i : i\in\mathcal{I}\} \text{ of the embedding matrix (selected token ids) are trainable; } E_0 \text{ otherwise frozen};\ \text{HF stores the trained rows themselves (init } = E_{0,\mathcal{I}}\text{) and writes them back with index\_copy}
methods.trainable_params: |\mathcal{I}|\cdot d
methods.locus: input embedding matrix rows for chosen token indices (optionally tied output embedding)
methods.structure: row-selection mask on the embedding matrix: \Delta E is supported on the rows indexed by \mathcal{I}
methods.mergeable_reason: The trained rows are written back into the embedding matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: New rows initialized to the current embeddings of those tokens, so the method is a no-op before training.
methods.key_idea: To add or retrain a few tokens, update only their embedding rows rather than the whole embedding matrix or a LoRA on it, saving memory and storage and leaving other tokens untouched.

relations.note: Can be used together with LoRA via trainable_token_indices.

methods.verification_notes: No paper or arXiv id; it exists as an HF PEFT tuner (tuners/trainable_tokens, TrainableTokensConfig, introduced in v0.15.0 released 2025-03-19, weight tying in PR #2399) and through LoraConfig(trainable_token_indices=...). Docs page package_reference/trainable_tokens confirmed.
corrections: formula_latex: noted that HF PEFT stores and overwrites the selected rows (index_copy) rather than storing deltas; this is equivalent to the row-supported delta.

papers.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
papers.claim: Dense randomly initialized networks contain sparse subnetworks ('winning tickets') that, trained in isolation from their original initialization, match the full network's accuracy; iterative magnitude pruning finds them.
papers.relevance: Supplies the train-select-rewind-retrain recipe behind LT-SFT and the general idea that a sparse sub-object of parameter space suffices, i.e. selection as a subobject/mask functor on parameter spaces.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1803.03635 (Frankle, 2018-03; journal-ref ICLR 2019) confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Training BatchNorm and Only BatchNorm: On the Expressive Power of Random Features in CNNs
papers.claim: Training only BatchNorm's affine parameters on top of frozen random weights reaches surprisingly high accuracy (e.g. 82% on CIFAR-10 for deep ResNets), far above training an equal number of random other parameters.
papers.relevance: Evidence that per-channel affine (diagonal scale/shift) parameters are disproportionately expressive, the foundation for BitFit, LN Tuning and (IA)^3-style diagonal methods.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2003.00152 (Frankle, 2020-02; comment 'Published in ICLR 2021') confirmed; 82% CIFAR-10 / 32% ImageNet top-5 matches the abstract.

papers.title: Delta Tuning: A Comprehensive Study of Parameter Efficient Methods for Pre-trained Language Models
papers.claim: Unifies PEFT as 'delta tuning' and classifies methods into addition-based, specification-based (selective) and reparameterization-based, with optimization and optimal-control perspectives and large-scale experiments.
papers.relevance: Its 'specification-based' class is exactly this family; the delta-on-parameters view is the starting point for treating PEFT methods as morphisms acting on parameter spaces.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2203.06904 (Ding, 2022-03) confirmed; the published version appeared in Nature Machine Intelligence 5 (2023) under the title 'Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large-scale pre-trained language models' (doi 10.1038/s42256-023-00626-4, Crossref). The addition / specification / reparameterization taxonomy matches the abstract.

papers.title: Scaling Down to Scale Up: A Guide to Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Surveys 50+ PEFT papers with a taxonomy of additive, selective, reparametrization-based and hybrid methods and benchmarks 15 methods, noting that sparse selective methods are of limited practicality on current hardware.
papers.relevance: Gives the standard 'selective' category (layer-depth, layer-type and individual-parameter selection) and the hardware critique that motivates structured selective methods (S2FT, SMT).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.15647 (Lialin, 2023-03; v2 2024) confirmed; no venue found, so arXiv. Over 50 papers, 15 benchmarked methods, depth/type/individual-parameter selective taxonomy and 'unrestricted unstructured sparsity is still impractical on contemporary hardware' all appear in v2.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Shows that random, rule-based and projection-based PEFT methods are all p-sparse fine-tuned models (with respect to an equivalent model for structure-changing methods) and proves that sparsity regularizes by bounding stability, which yields generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: A theorem-level unification of PEFT under the selective view (theta = theta_0 + M Delta theta), directly usable as the 'mask' object in a categorical account; also motivates the SAM selection method.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2211.15583 (Fu, 2022-11) confirmed; AAAI 2023 via Crossref (doi 10.1609/aaai.v37i11.26505); random/rule-based/projection-based categorization and stability-based generalization bound match the abstract.

papers.title: Task-Specific Skill Localization in Fine-tuned Language Models
papers.claim: Grafting the fine-tuned values of a tiny subset (~0.01%) of parameters onto the pretrained model recovers over 95% of the fine-tuned model's performance; such grafted regions localize task skills and help continual learning.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that fine-tuning deltas are effectively sparse, supporting selective PEFT and composition of sparse deltas (as in LT-SFT).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2302.06600 (Panigrahi, 2023-02; comment 'ICML 2023') confirmed in PMLR v202 (panigrahi23a); ~0.01% of parameters, >95% performance matches the abstract.

papers.title: What Would Elsa Do? Freezing Layers During Transformer Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Fine-tuning only the final quarter of BERT/RoBERTa layers (3-5 of 12 in base models) retains about 90% of full fine-tuning quality.
papers.relevance: Early quantification of layer-depth selection, the coarse end of the selective family (top-k layer tuning, surgical fine-tuning, LISA).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1911.03090 (Lee, Jaejun; 2019-11; 5-page arXiv note) confirmed; no venue found, so arXiv. 'Only a fourth of the final layers ... 90% of the original quality' matches the abstract.

notes: Scope: methods whose trainable object is a subset of the pretrained parameters, W = W_0 + M ⊙ ΔW with a 0/1 support M, including hand-specified supports (BitFit, BEFT, LN Tuning, Trainable Tokens, surgical/top-layer tuning), data-driven fixed masks (FISH Mask, Child-Tuning_D, SAM, SIFT, GPS, SPT, SHiRA, PaFi, LIFT, Super-Tuning), learned or dynamic supports (Diff Pruning, LT-SFT, SpIEL), structured supports (S2FT head/channel slices, SMT tiles, GPS row-balanced) and time-varying layer selection (LISA, HiFT, BAdam, Child-Tuning_F) which are tagged optimizer-or-training-procedure because their accumulated update is dense. Masking/Piggyback learn a multiplicative 0/1 mask on W_0 and are tagged multiplicative-weight (dual of selective deltas). SPT and RoSA are sparse+low-rank hybrids. Seed check: all 16 seeds exist and are included; 'SMT' is the ICLR 2025 paper whose arXiv title is 'Sparse Matrix in Large Language Model Fine-tuning'. HF PEFT (main branch, checked 2026-10-01) contains four selective tuners: LNTuningConfig, ShiraConfig, BeftConfig, TrainableTokensConfig, plus SupertuningConfig (2026). BitFit has no dedicated config (LoraConfig(bias='all') only trains biases alongside LoRA), so hf_peft=false. Cross-family relation targets used: lora, dora, ia3, galore, mezo, mad-x (these ids should exist in other family files; mad-x may be named differently). Uncertainties: Super-Tuning (arXiv 2607.09287, July 2026) is very recent with negligible citations, included because it ships in HF PEFT; its HF implementation uses magnitude scoring while the paper's headline uses Wanda scores. Trainable Tokens has no paper; year 2025 inferred from PEFT v0.15.0 release notes. SpIEL appears to remain arXiv-only. S2FT's exact sliced matrices (rows vs columns) depend on weight-layout convention, so the formula states them generically. Omitted as lower-uptake or out of scope: SparseGrad (EMNLP 2024), GMT gradient-mask tuning (AAAI 2025), Partial Fine-Tuning for ViTs (2023), SpaRTA random sparse adaptation (2025), NeFT neuron-level tuning, TinyTL (bias + lite residual, hybrid), DiffFit, LN-tuning of Qi et al. 2022 (arXiv 2211.08682, cited inside the ln-tuning entry), FRoD (HF PEFT, not selective).
verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of all 26 methods and 7 papers. Metadata: all 31 arXiv ids were fetched in one export-API batch; titles, first authors and first-version years all match. SMT's arXiv title differs from its ICLR 2025 title. Venues were confirmed through arXiv comments/journal-refs, ACL Anthology (8 pages), the NeurIPS 2021/2024 proceedings listings (FISH, LISA, S2FT, SHiRA, BAdam), the ICLR 2023/2024/2025 virtual sites (Surgical, LN Tuning, SMT, which also give the OpenReview ids), PMLR v202/v235/v267 (Panigrahi, SIFT, RoSA, LIFT) and Crossref (Piggyback ECCV 2018, SAM AAAI 2023, GPS CVPR 2024, SPT ICCV 2023, Delta Tuning NMI 2023 under a different title). SpIEL, Super-Tuning, Lialin et al. and Elsa stay arXiv. Formulas were checked against the arXiv HTML full text of every method paper. Fixes: SPT sensitivity sums g^2 over C = 800 samples. SAM squares the gradient summed over 500-2000 burn-in steps, so it differs from a Fisher score. LIFT refreshes its mask from SVD_r of the current weights. RoSA builds its mask after a 64-batch LoRA warm-up and alpha is in {1,2}. LT-SFT freezes the output embedding and LayerNorm, not the embeddings. Global-vs-per-matrix parameter counts were corrected for FISH, Child-Tuning_D, LT-SFT and SAM; d_v replaces d for BEFT under GQA; LN Tuning's 0.004% was checked. HF PEFT (main, v0.21.1, tuners dir via GitHub API, docs pages checked): LNTuningConfig, ShiraConfig (v0.17.0), BeftConfig (v0.20.0), SupertuningConfig (v0.21.0) and TrainableTokensConfig (v0.15.0, also LoraConfig(trainable_token_indices)) are confirmed; no other method here is supported, including BitFit. HF Super-Tuning defaults to |W| TopK, while the paper's best sparse rows are BottomK. Mergeability and identity flags were unchanged apart from wording; Masking's 5% initial sparsity is now explicit. Relations: retyped 5 (spt->fish-mask, hift<->badam, shira->fish-mask, sam-sparse->fish-mask), removed 3 (lt-sft->spiel wrong direction, piggyback->masking wrong direction, surgical->bitfit unjustified) and added lift->sift. All targets are kebab-case slugs that exist in some family file. Nothing was dropped. 37 field-level corrections in total.
